standard_prerequisites.name: Direct sums described by four morphisms
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the characterization of a direct sum by four morphisms satisfying the identities, which is how the splitting is recognised.

core_obligations: The two splitting identities (proof lines 658-661): the lemma on the kernel and cokernel of an idempotent supplies p i equal to the identity on the kernel of f (and on the cokernel of f, which is the same object) and q j equal to the identity on the kernel of g (and on the cokernel of g).

The decomposition of the identity (proof lines 662-663): by construction the sum of the two composites i p and j q is f + g, which is the identity of the object x, so the four morphisms satisfy exactly the identities characterizing a direct sum; the four displayed isomorphisms then follow from the characterization.
proof_roadmap: Recall the identities supplied by the lemma on the kernel and cokernel of an idempotent.
Use the construction of the four morphisms to write the identity of the object as a sum of two composites.
Apply the characterization of a direct sum by four morphisms.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that when an idempotent endomorphism and its complement each have at least one of a kernel or a cokernel, all four exist and the object splits as a direct sum of any choice of one kernel or cokernel of the idempotent and one kernel or cokernel of its complement, with the structure given by the four constructed morphisms (statement lines 638-656). The proof is a complete argument: the two splitting identities are read off from the lemma on the kernel and cokernel of an idempotent (proof lines 658-661), and the construction makes the sum of the two composites equal to the identity, so the four morphisms satisfy the characterizing identities of a direct sum and the displayed isomorphisms follow (proof lines 662-663). The non-formal content is the verification of the identities of a direct sum. The claim is H2: a structured input with each input named.
